name: Arrabar
summary: "Shining Arrabar", capital of Chondath and a deep-water port metropolis on the south-eastern shore of the Vilhon Reach, at the end of the Golden Road and the Emerald Corridor; a walled, oval city of Port, Warehouse, Merchants and Living districts around the Governor District and the gold-domed Generon palace, with a canal quarter (the Netherwaters) behind its docks. Known for crime and corruption in the 14th century DR, ruled by the Lord of Arrabar and a ring of merchant houses, ruined in the Spellplague (1385 DR) and described as back on the map by the late 15th century DR.

climate.label: Warm, humid, subtropical
climate.scope: Regional figures for the Vilhon Reach, not readings specific to Arrabar

seasons.spring: Days can reach 80°F / 27°C; evenings and early mornings rarely drop below 60°F / 16°C. Arrives early Mirtul.
seasons.summer: High humidity, with heat reaching 110°F / 43°C. Begins when the druids' Long Night ends in early Eleasis.
seasons.autumn: Cooler; daytime highs range from 80°F down to 50°F (27 to 10°C). Approaches late Marpenoth.
seasons.winter: Heavy rain; usual highs of 50 to 65°F (10 to 18°C); cold spells can reach 35°F / 2°C; snow is rare.

inferences: City art: shaded streets, light clothing, lush planting, and buildings suited to heat and heavy rain.
The Netherwaters would likely feel damp and cooler than the streets above.

districts.name: Port District

uncertain_readings: District edges and sizes are read by eye from the plan; the sources give sides and plan numbers only
Marker spots for the taverns, eatery, Academia, Waukeen temple and cheese shop come from the wiki text, not the plan
The plan draws no canals; the sketch's canal grid is schematic
The Tempus temple text (eastern edge of the Governor's District) and plan (block 7 west of the Governor block) disagree
Which source the stored plans come from is unconfirmed; Arrabar_map.webp may be the wiki's "Arrabar map BW.jpg" (credited to The Ruby Guardian map)
The generated images in the folder follow the earlier sketch and do not match the plan (Generon at the centre, Warehouse District along the whole north)

Greenwood (2022) reconciles the Crying Claw: canals run far inland, so the tavern has both a boat entrance and a street entrance; the wiki's fishing rule (boats, shores, balconies) is wider than his (boats only)
plan_features: Oval ring road around a walled, block-by-block city on the Reach shore; north is up
Piers along the west (sea) edge, in the Port District
Port District 1 is the western strip; Warehouse blocks 2 fill the north-west; Merchants blocks 3 lie in the south; Governor block 4 is the central block; Living blocks 5 fill the east
The Generon (6) is the walled compound at the top of the central block, north of the Governor block, with Warehouse blocks to its west and Living blocks to its east
Temple blocks 9 (Lliira), 7 (Tempus) and 8 (Silvanus) lie together just south-west of the centre, between the Port strip and the Governor block and above the Merchants blocks
Emerald Corridor leaves from the east side toward Iljak; the Golden Road leaves from the south, heading south-south-west toward Ormpetarr, and runs through the city as its main diagonal street
Small buildings (noble manors) stand outside the walls around the ring road
The atlas image carries a 0 to 500 ft bar on which the walled blocks measure about 1,300 to 1,500 ft across, too small for the stated population; the scale is not relied on

greenwood_2022_canals.in_reply_to: Question from @Artie_Pavlov (2022-01-05): the Crying Claw is said to be on the waterfront, but the novels and novel map put it two districts from the Reach
points: Port District honeycombed with canals leading to a large turning basin just south of the Warehouse District
Many buildings are "waterfront" yet look several streets inland on the stylized published maps; the Crying Claw can be reached by boat

Almost all canals are roofed over; a light well, smaller than the basin, opens onto it; buildings have deep cellars; streets run on the roofs; rain drains through gratings (compared to modern Chicago Loop)
Narrowboat barges take garbage out to sea and down the coast for dumping in the Shallows, a noisome monster-infested bay
City polices the canals heavily because competitors would block them to delay rivals
Fishing from boats is banned in the canals and basin; fishing with a rod from a balcony or window is contrasted as allowed; rumoured aquatic monsters
Canals, docks and basin are the Netherwaters, shortened to Nethers or Below; low, criminal and misshapen people live and work there, and many Arrabarrans never mention it

regional_relations: Hlath: single governor under Arrabar control; highway link
Iljak: pays heavy taxes, serves Lord Wianar, exports crops and grain to Arrabar
Samra and Mussum: paid taxes to Arrabar; Shamph lumber dispersed through Arrabar, Samra and Mussum
Sespech: broke away after the Rotting War; puppet barons until 1364 DR; Haskar Corintis financed; invasion planned by 1372 DR
Elbulder: turned back an Arrabarran band
Mimph: razed 135 DR; later rivalry and cargo seizures at sea
Lachom: disdained Arrabar; traded with Surkh
Free cities: worked together to stop Arrabar regaining its old strength
Golden Road: Arrabar through Ormpetarr to Innarlith, Shaarmid and Kormul; Fort Arran between Sespech and Arrabar
Chondath: one of the most densely populated nations; Arrabar the largest city (Atlas of Ice and Fire)
